([[Memphis, Tennessee]]) | college = * [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] (2020–2021) * [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] (2021–2023) * [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]] (2023–2024) * Memphis (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team2 = →[[Texas Legends]] | highlights = * [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] champion ([[2021 National Invitation Tournament|2021]]) * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] co-Defensive Player of the Year (2022) * 2× Big 12 All-Defensive Team (2022, 2023) * [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|AAC Freshman of the Year]] (2021) * AAC All-Freshman Team (2021) * [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] (2020) }} '''Moussa Cissé''' (born 10 September 2002) is a Guinean professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]], [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss Rebels]] and the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best [[center (basketball)|centers]] in the 2020 class. ==Early life== Cissé was born in [[Conakry]], Guinea, and lived there until age 14, when he moved to [[New York City|New York]].{{cite web |last1=Varlas |first1=John |title=When it comes to Lausanne's Moussa Cisse, seeing is believing |url=https://dailymemphian.com/section/sports/article/9560/when-it-comes-to-lausannes-moussa-cisse-seeing-is |website=The Daily Memphian |access-date=27 May 2020 |date=19 December 2019}} He had grown up playing [[association football|soccer]].{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Touted basketball recruit Moussa Cisse reclassifying to 2020 class |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29229093/touted-recruit-moussa-cisse-reclassifying-2020-class |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=27 May 2020 |date=27 May 2020}} Cissé started playing high school basketball for [[St. Benedict's Preparatory School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]], playing alongside [[Precious Achiuwa]].{{cite web |last1=Munz |first1=Jason |title=Five-star Moussa Cisse commits to Memphis basketball, bolstering Penny Hardaway's frontcourt |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/07/15/moussa-cisse-commits-memphis-basketball-penny-hardaway/5274634002/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=15 July 2020 |date=15 July 2020}} For two years, he played for [[Christ the King Regional High School]] in [[Queens, New York|Queens]], where he was teammates with [[Kofi Cockburn]].{{cite web |last1=Cordova |first1=David |title=Christ the King Stakes Their Royal Claim Around The City |url=https://davesjoint.net/2018/01/21/christ-the-king-stakes-their-royal-claim-around-the-city/ |publisher=Dave's Joint |access-date=27 May 2020 |date=21 January 2018}} As a sophomore, Cissé led his team to the Class AA state title game.{{cite web |last1=Thompson |first1=Khari |title=Moussa Cisse's dominant second half leads Lausanne to Division II-A state title |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/03/07/high-school-basketball-moussa-cisse-leads-lauasanne-tssaa-state-ttile/4928276002/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=27 May 2020 |date=7 March 2020}} For his junior season, he transferred to [[Lausanne Collegiate School]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]].{{cite web |last1=Thompson |first1=Khari |title=High school basketball: 5-star forward Moussa Cisse transferring to Lausanne |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/08/14/moussa-cisse-transferring-memphis-lausanne/2011427001/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=27 May 2020 |date=14 August 2019}} On 25 November 2019, Cissé recorded 31 points, 22 rebounds and 21 blocks, surpassing the [[Shelby County, Tennessee|Shelby County]] single-game blocks record held by Mitch Omar since 1976–77. He led Lausanne to the Division II-A state championship, where he was named [[most valuable player]] after posting 15 points, 10 rebounds and nine blocks against [[First Assembly Christian School]]. As a junior, Cissé averaged 18.4 points, 15.3 rebounds and 9.2 blocks per game, earning Division II-A [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] honors. He broke [[Michael Wilson (basketball)|Michael Wilson]]'s single-season city record for blocks per game set in 1989–90. ===Recruiting=== Cissé was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], according to major recruiting services, and was considered a top 10 player in the 2021 recruiting class.{{cite web |last1=Benjamin |first1=Daniel |title=NCAA Basketball: Top 10 prospect Moussa Cisse considering reclassifing, down to 10 |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2020/04/17/ncaa-basketball-top-10-prospect-moussa-cisse-considering-reclassifing-10/ |publisher=Busting Brackets |access-date=27 May 2020 |date=17 April 2020}} On 27 May 2020, he announced that he would graduate from high school a year early and [[reclassification (education)|reclassify]] to the 2020 class, where he remained a five-star recruit. On 15 July, Cissé committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]]. He was drawn to the program by head coach [[Penny Hardaway]] and former high school teammate Precious Achiuwa, who had played for Memphis in the previous season.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=No. 24-rated prospect Moussa Cisse commits to Memphis basketball |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29468237/no-24-rated-prospect-moussa-cisse-commits-memphis-basketball |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=15 July 2020 |date=15 July 2020}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Moussa Cissé | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Conakry|Conakry, Guinea]] | highschool = [[Lausanne Collegiate School]] (TN) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 220 | 40 = | commitdate = 15 July 2020 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 92 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = Memphis 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 Memphis Tigers Recruiting Class | rivals school = memphis | scout s = | espn schoolid = 235 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 14 | 247 overall = 12 | espn overall = 24 | accessdate = 7 August 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== At Memphis, Cissé posted his first double-double on 2 December 2020, scoring 14 points and securing 10 rebounds in an 83–54 victory over [[Arkansas State Red Wolves men's basketball|Arkansas State]].{{cite news |title=Nolley II carries Memphis over Arkansas St. 83–54 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401258889 |access-date=18 July 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=2 December 2020}} In his freshman year, he averaged 6.6 points, 6.3 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game, earning [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|American Athletic Conference Freshman of the Year]] honors. On 6 April 2021, Cissé declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Fowler |first1=Christian |title=Moussa Cisse declares for 2021 NBA Draft, maintains NCAA eligibility |url=https://247sports.com/college/memphis/Article/Moussa-Cisse-declares-for-2021-NBA-Draft-maintains-NCAA-eligibility-163488931/ |access-date=19 July 2021 |work=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |date=6 April 2021}} He later withdrew from the draft and entered the transfer portal. On 15 July 2021, he transferred to [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], choosing the Cowboys over [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Moussa Cisse transferring to Oklahoma State after one season of Memphis basketball |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31822004/moussa-cisse-transferring-oklahoma-state-one-year-memphis |access-date=18 July 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=15 July 2021}} In his sophomore year, Cissé was named [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Co-Defensive Player of the Year, alongside [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]]’s [[Jonathan Tchamwa Tchatchoua]] and [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]]’s Gabe Osabuohien.{{cite news |last1=Lederman |first1=Eli |title=Cisse named Big 12 Co-Defensive Player of the Year; OSU's Anderson, OU's Noland earn conference honors |url=https://tulsaworld.com/sports/college/osu/cisse-named-big-12-co-defensive-player-of-the-year-osus-anderson-ous-noland-earn/article_c3f2526c-9dc2-11ec-9baf-b32786c8a172.html |access-date=11 March 2022 |work=[[Tulsa World]] |date=6 March 2022}} He averaged 7.2 points, 6.5 rebounds and 1.9 blocks per game.{{cite news |last1=Unruh |first1=Jacob |title=Oklahoma State star center Moussa Cisse announces return for 2022–23 season |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/college/cowboys/2022/03/11/moussa-cisse-oklahoma-state-basketball-return-next-season-cowboys/7006147001/ |access-date=6 March 2023 |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |date=11 March 2022}} As a junior, he was named to the Big 12 All-Defensive Team.{{cite news |last1=Nagel |first1=Cody |title=Oklahoma State forwards Kalib Boone, Moussa Cisse earn All-Big 12 honors |url=https://247sports.com/college/oklahoma-state/Article/oklahoma-state-basketball-forwards-kalib-boone-moussa-cisse-earn-all-big-12-honors-205811507/ |access-date=6 March 2023 |work=247 Sports |date=5 March 2023}} After the 2022–23 season Cissé entered the transfer portal for a second time, later committing to play for [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]] over offers from [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] and [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]].{{Cite web |date=14 May 2023 |title=Center Cisse commits to transfer to Ole Miss |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/37647745/center-moussa-cisse-commits-transfer-ole-miss |access-date=13 August 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} For the 2024–25 season, Cissé transferred back to Memphis.{{cite web|url=https://gotigersgo.com/news/2024/6/7/mens-basketball-moussa-cisse-returns-home|title=Moussa Cisse Returns Home|work=Memphis Tigers|date=7 June 2024|accessdate=13 May 2025}} ==Professional career== On 8 July 2025, Cissé was signed by the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web|title=Mavs ink contracts with Moussa Cisse and Matthew Cleveland|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavssigncisseandcleveland/|date=8 July 2025|access-date=8 July 2025|website=mavs.com}} On 18 October, the Mavericks converted Cissé's contract into a [[two-way contract]].{{Cite web|title=Moussa Cisse, through energy and effort, earns a spot on Mavericks' season-opening roster|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2025/10/18/dallas-mavericks-roster-moussa-cisse-jason-kidd/|access-date=24 October 2025|website=dallasnews.com|language=en}} In Dallas' season finale on 12 April 2026 against the [[2025–26 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]], Cissé logged career-highs in points (17) and rebounds (20).{{Cite web|title=Mavericks' Moussa Cisse: Grabs 20 rebounds in season finale|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/mavericks-moussa-cisse-grabs-20-rebounds-in-season-finale/|access-date=July 31, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} Cisse was re-signed to a two-year contract on July 22, 2026.{{Cite web |date=July 22, 2026 |title=Mavericks Sign Moussa Cissé|url=https://www.nba.com/mavs/news/mavericks-sign-moussa-cisse|access-date=July 22, 2026 |website=mavs.com}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular
